input: my kettle is full of limescale, how do i get rid of it

In a hard-water area do it every couple of months: the scale forms because hard water leaves calcium behind as it boils, and a thick layer makes the kettle slow and puts a scum on the tea.

reply: Hi there — what do you need?

Do one small thing you used to enjoy today, at half enthusiasm, because mood follows action more often than it arrives on its own: a walk to the shop, a phone call, ten minutes of a game you liked. Then stack the three things that lift a low mood most reliably - daylight within an hour of waking, 20 minutes of walking, and one person you really talk to rather than message - and keep bedtime and meals at the same time, because a sad week wrecks both and then feeds itself. Write one line a day about how it went, so you can see it is not all bad. If it is most days for two weeks, if the pleasure has gone out of everything, or if it is stopping you eating or working, take it to the GP: talking therapy works, and in most areas you can refer yourself.

input: my kettle is full of limescale, how do i get rid of it
reply: Half fill the kettle with equal parts water and white vinegar, or a sachet of citric acid, boil it and leave it half an hour, then tip it out and boil fresh water twice before you use it again. In a hard-water area do it every couple of months: the scale forms because hard water leaves calcium behind as it boils, and a thick layer makes the kettle slow and puts a scum on the tea.

input: how do i organize my fridge
reply: Eat in date order first, and after that the food that is on borrowed time: fresh fish and mince within a day or two, then soft fruit, berries and salad leaves, then milk, yoghurt and cream, then hard cheese, butter and cooked leftovers. Where it sits matters as much as the order - cooked and ready-to-eat food on the top shelves, raw meat and fish on the bottom shelf in a box so nothing drips, and vegetables in the drawer. The door is the warmest part, so keep milk out of it, and the top of the door is fine for butter and condiments.

input: how often should i water my tomato plants
reply: Tomatoes want about two to three litres each, twice a week in dry weather, poured at the base in the morning so the leaves are dry by night. Anything in a pot needs water every day in summer, and beans, courgettes, cucumbers and potatoes want a good can each in a dry spell. Steady watering matters more than the exact amount: up and down watering is what splits tomatoes and causes blossom end rot. Rain of more than a few millimetres counts, and a mulch holds the moisture you have given them.

input: how do i Clean a cast iron pan
reply: Scrub it with hot water and a stiff brush or a handful of coarse salt while it is still warm, then dry it on the hob over a low heat: a little washing-up liquid is fine, but soaking it is what strips the seasoning. input: wyh does my smûke alarm keep  beeping
reply: A chirp every minute or so is the low-battery warning: twist the alarm off its base, swap the battery (usually a 9V, sometimes AA) and press the test button until it sounds properly. Mains-powered alarms have a backup cell that does the same thing, and any alarm over ten years old wants replacing whole rather than mending.

What it does do is leave a chalky film on taps, kettles and shower glass, lather soap and shampoo less so you use more of them, and feel drier on the skin - a filter jug or a scale reducer is enough for most homes. reply: A night runs in cycles of about ninety minutes: light sleep, then deeper sleep, then a stretch of REM where you dream, and round again.
